mainTopic: The ברייתא's list of who gets מיתה בידי שמים: a זר who eats תרומה, and the sources for each disqualified כהן who serves
overview: The גמרא goes through a ברייתא that lists who gets מיתה בידי שמים. It first finishes explaining why a טמא כהן who eats טמאה תרומה is not liable: that תרומה is already desecrated. For a זר who eats תרומה, רב says he gets only מלקות, since 'אני ה׳ מקדשם' ends the topic of death. When the ברייתא is raised against him, the גמרא answers that רב תנא הוא ופליג. Next, a זר who serves gets death from 'והזר הקרב יומת'. A טמא כהן who serves gets death through a גזירה שוה of חילול from תרומה. The גמרא asks why we don't learn from נותר instead, and it settles the question because plural matches plural. A טבול יום, a מחוסר בגדים, a מחוסר כפרה, a כהן who did not wash, a drunk כהן, and one with overgrown hair each get a source for death. Finally, the ברייתא says an ערל, an אונן, and one who serves sitting are only under an אזהרה, and רב חסדא begins showing that the source for the ערל comes from יחזקאל, a quote that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Already-desecrated תרומה is excluded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the earlier derivation: a טמא כהן who eats טמאה תרומה is not liable to death, because that תרומה is already desecrated.
steps.simpleTranslation: This excludes תרומה that is already desecrated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing the discussion from just before. It explains which case the פסוק leaves out: תרומה that has already become טמאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The death penalty for a טמא כהן eating תרומה comes from the words 'ומתו בו כי יחללוהו', which means he dies for desecrating it. If the תרומה is already טמאה, it is already desecrated, so eating it does not desecrate it again. That is why there is no מיתה בידי שמים in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: to the exclusion of; this leaves out
desecrated; it has lost its holy status
and stands that way already; it is already in that state

phrases.english: to the exclusion of this one
phrases.notes: 'This one' is תרומה that is already טמאה, from the case just discussed.

phrases.english: that is already desecrated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the derivation that started before this section of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A טמא כהן who eats טמאה תרומה is not liable to מיתה בידי שמים, because that תרומה is already desecrated.

steps.title: רב says a non-כהן who eats תרומה gets lashes
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists a זר who ate תרומה among those who get death. רב rules that he gets מלקות instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא lists 'a זר who ate תרומה' as liable to death. רב says: a זר who ate תרומה gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the ברייתא, a זר who ate תרומה. רב gives a different ruling: the punishment is מלקות, not death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts this case on its list of מיתה בידי שמים. רב says the punishment is only מלקות. This sets up the next steps, where רב has to defend his view.

keyTerms.meaning: a non-כהן
the holy portion of produce given to a כהן
gets lashes (מלקות)

steps.confusionAlert: The first words, 'וזר שאכל את התרומה', are the ברייתא's line, and the ברייתא says death. Only after 'אמר רב' do we hear רב's different ruling of lashes.

phrases.english: And a non-priest who ate teruma,
Rav said:
A non-priest who ate teruma is flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזָר שֶׁאָכַל אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, a זר who eats תרומה gets מלקות, not מיתה בידי שמים.

steps.title: רב כהנא and רב אסי point to a פסוק that seems to mean death
steps.stepSummary: רב's students ask: shouldn't it be death? The פסוק 'וכל זר לא יאכל קדש' comes right after a פסוק about dying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב: Let the master say he gets death, since it is written, 'No non-priest shall eat of the holy'.
steps.whatsHappening: Two of רב's students challenge his ruling. They bring a פסוק that seems to show the punishment is death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right before 'וכל זר לא יאכל קדש', the תורה says 'ומתו בו' about a טמא כהן eating תרומה. Because the two פסוקים sit next to each other, the students want to give the זר the same punishment of death.

keyTerms.meaning: let the master say; shouldn't you say
with death (מיתה בידי שמים)
holy food; here it means תרומה

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:
Let the Master say he is punished with death,
as it is written: “No non-priest shall eat of the sacred”?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:10. The פסוק right before it (22:9) talks about dying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling of lashes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a זר who eats תרומה gets only מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The זר פסוק sits right next to 'ומתו בו', so it should share the same punishment of death.

steps.title: 'אני ה׳ מקדשם' separates the two topics
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the words 'אני ה׳ מקדשם' close the earlier topic, so the death penalty does not carry over to the זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I am ה׳ who sanctifies them' interrupts the topic.
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends himself. The phrase 'אני ה׳ מקדשם' comes between the two פסוקים and ends the topic of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students' argument depends on the two פסוקים being one connected topic. רב says the closing words of פסוק 9 cut the connection. So the זר's case stands alone, and the plain לאו gives only מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: it interrupted the topic; it ended the subject
who makes them holy

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא blocks learning from nearby פסוקים: a break in between stops one topic from carrying over to the next.

phrases.english: “I am the Lord Who sanctifies them” —
phrases.notes: These words end ויקרא 22:9, right before the זר פסוק begins.

phrases.english: interrupted the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Breaking the link between the two פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The זר learns from 'ומתו בו' in the פסוק next to it and gets death.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אני ה׳ מקדשם' closes the topic, so the זר does not get death, only מלקות.

steps.title: The ברייתא says death, against רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב from the ברייתא, which openly lists a זר who eats תרומה among those who get death.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'And these are the ones who get death: a non-priest who eats תרומה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב again, this time from a ברייתא instead of a פסוק. The ברייתא clearly says a זר who eats תרומה gets death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב answered the challenge from the פסוק, but now an earlier source rules against him outright. Normally an אמורא cannot argue with a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (from an earlier source)
and these are the ones

phrases.english: They raised an objection: And these are the ones who are liable to death —
a non-priest who eats teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רב from a ברייתא, after he answered the challenge from the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא openly says death, and an אמורא normally may not disagree with a ברייתא.

steps.title: רב is a תנא and may disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב has the standing of a תנא, so he is allowed to disagree with the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are raising a contradiction from a ברייתא against רב? רב is a תנא and he disagrees!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. It does not explain the ברייתא differently; it says רב is allowed to disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was an early אמורא who was given the standing of a תנא. So a ברייתא is not a final proof against him. The result is a real disagreement between רב and the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא (a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה)
you are throwing at; you are raising a contradiction
a sage of the משנה period
and he disagrees

steps.whatToRemember: A זר who eats תרומה: according to the ברייתא he gets מיתה בידי שמים; according to רב he gets מלקות, because 'אני ה׳ מקדשם' ends the topic of death. רב may disagree with the ברייתא because רב תנא הוא ופליג.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'רב תנא הוא ופליג' is a standard answer across ש״ס whenever a ברייתא contradicts רב.

phrases.english: Are you raising a contradiction from a baraita against Rav?
Rav is a tanna, and he disagrees!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתָא אַדְּרַב קָא רָמֵית? רַב תַּנָּא הוּא וּפָלֵיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Authority: רב has the standing of a תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ברייתא refutes רב, since an אמורא cannot argue with a תנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב counts as a תנא, so he may hold a different view from the ברייתא.

steps.title: A non-כהן who does the עבודה gets death
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a זר who did the עבודה in the מקדש gets מיתה בידי שמים, from 'והזר הקרב יומת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a non-priest who served, as it is written: 'And the non-priest who comes near shall be put to death.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's list and explains its next case. A זר who did the עבודה gets death, and the גמרא gives the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, unlike the תרומה case, the פסוק itself says 'יומת', so the source for death is clear. This is a new case on the list, not part of the argument with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: served; did the עבודה in the מקדש
who comes near (to do the עבודה)
shall be put to death

phrases.english: And a non-priest who performed the service,
as it is written: “And the non-priest who approaches shall be put to death.”
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's list and moves to its next case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זר who does the עבודה in the מקדש is liable to מיתה בידי שמים, from 'והזר הקרב יומת'.

steps.title: The ברייתא adds a טמא כהן who did the עבודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's list continues: a טמא כהן who served in the מקדש also gets מיתה בידי שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a טמא כהן who did the עבודה also gets death by the hands of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more case to its list of people who get מיתה בידי שמים: a כהן who was טמא and still did the עבודה. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא looks for the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 gave the case of a זר who did the עבודה. Now the ברייתא gives a different person: a real כהן who did the עבודה while he was טמא. The punishment is the same, death by the hands of Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure
Served, meaning he did the עבודה in the מקדש

phrases.english: And an impure [כהן] who served,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טמא כהן who did the עבודה gets מיתה בידי שמים.

steps.title: רב חייא בר אבין asks רב יוסף for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a question that רב חייא בר אבין asked רב יוסף: where do we learn that a טמא כהן who served gets death?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב חייא בר אבין asked רב יוסף: From where do we know that a טמא כהן who served gets death?
steps.whatsHappening: To find the source for the ברייתא's ruling, the גמרא brings a question that one אמורא asked another. This sets up רב יוסף's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not doubting the rule. It only asks which פסוק teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: As he asked of him
From where do we know?

phrases.aramaic: כְּדִבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מֵרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: As Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin asked of Rav Yosef:
From where [do we know] that an impure [כהן] who served
is [punished] with death?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מֵרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of the ruling in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that a טמא כהן who served gets מיתה?

steps.title: רב יוסף's source: a פסוק plus a גזירה שוה from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes the פסוק 'ולא יחללו את שם קדשי' and learns the death penalty through a גזירה שוה on the word חילול from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Speak to אהרן and his sons, that they keep away from the holy things of בני ישראל and not desecrate My holy name.' And the תנא learns 'desecration' from 'desecration' by תרומה: just as there the punishment is death, so too here it is death.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers in two parts. First he shows a פסוק that forbids a טמא כהן to serve and calls it חילול. Then he links that word to the word חילול by תרומה, where the punishment is death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק by itself gives a prohibition but no punishment. The גזירה שוה carries the punishment over: the same word חילול appears by a טמא כהן eating תרומה, and that one gets death. So the טמא כהן who served also gets death.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall keep away
Desecration, the key word of the גזירה שוה
Learning a law from one place to another through a word that appears in both
The portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a גזירה שוה works: the shared word lets the punishment written in one place apply to the other place.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"Speak to Aaron and to his sons
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:2

phrases.english: that they shall keep away from the holy things of the children of Israel
and they shall not desecrate My holy name."
And he learns "desecration" "desecration" from תרומה,
phrases.notes: "He" is the תנא of the ברייתא. By תרומה the פסוק says 'ומתו בו כי יחללהו' (ויקרא 22:9).

phrases.english: just as there [it is] with death –
so too here [it is] with death.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: דַּבֵּר אֶל אַהֲרֹן וְאֶל בָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ולא יחללו, together with a גזירה שוה of חילול from תרומה, teaches מיתה.

steps.title: Why not learn from נותר and give כרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the word חילול also appears by נותר, where the punishment is כרת, so why not learn from there?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn 'desecration' from 'desecration' by נותר: just as there the punishment is כרת, so too here it should be כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice of תרומה. The same word חילול also appears by נותר, and that would give a different punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה depends on a shared word, and here the shared word shows up in two places with two different punishments. If we learned from נותר, the טמא כהן who served would get כרת instead of מיתה. So the גמרא needs a reason to prefer תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us learn (instead)
Meat of a קרבן left over past its time
Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven different from מיתה

phrases.english: But let us learn "desecration" "desecration" from נותר:
phrases.notes: By נותר the פסוק says 'כי את קדש ה׳ חלל ונכרת' (ויקרא 19:8).

phrases.english: just as there [it is] כרת,
so too here [it should be] כרת?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the גזירה שוה of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of תרומה as the source of the גזירה שוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word חילול also appears by נותר, which has כרת, so the punishment could just as well be כרת.

steps.title: תרומה is the better match: four shared features
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it makes more sense to learn from תרומה, since it shares four features with our case: גוף, טמא, מקוה, and plural wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that he should learn from תרומה, because the two cases share: the body, impurity, a מקוה, and the plural.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It lists four ways that a טמא כהן eating תרומה is more like a טמא כהן serving than נותר is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גוף: in both cases the problem is in the כהן's own body, not in the food. טמא: both cases are about impurity. מקוה: in both, going to the מקוה fixes the problem. ברבים: in both, the word חילול is written in the plural, while by נותר it is in the singular. Since תרומה matches on all four, we learn from it, and the punishment is מיתה.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it is reasonable
Body: the problem is in the person himself
Ritual bath that removes impurity
In the plural

steps.confusionAlert: The four words are not four separate laws. Each one is a way that תרומה is similar to our case and נותר is not.

phrases.english: It is reasonable that he should learn from תרומה,
since [they share]: body, impure,
phrases.notes: In both cases the problem is in the כהן himself, because he is טמא. By נותר the problem is in the meat.

phrases.english: a מקוה, the plural.
phrases.notes: A מקוה fixes both cases. 'יחללו' and 'ומתו... יחללהו' are plural, while by נותר 'חלל' is singular.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picking between two possible sources by counting shared features
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word חילול could point to נותר just as well, which would give כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומה matches on גוף, טמא, מקוה, and ברבים, so we learn from it, and the punishment is מיתה.

steps.title: Pushback: maybe we should learn from leftover offerings instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the other way: נותר also shares four features with a טמא כהן who served, namely קודש, פנים, פיגול and נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! He should have learned from נותר, since it shares these features with our case: it is about holy sacrifices, it happens inside the מקדש, and both פיגול and נותר apply to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 12. It says נותר has just as many things in common with our case as תרומה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 chose תרומה because it shares four features with a טמא כהן who served. Now the גמרא shows that נותר also shares four features: it deals with קודש, it happens in the מקדש (פנים), and the rules of פיגול and נותר apply. So the count is a tie, and the choice of תרומה is no longer obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite makes more sense
Holy sacrificial matters
Inside the מקדש
A קרבן ruined by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten

phrases.english: On the contrary, from leftover offerings (נותר)
he should have learned it,
since it shares: holy sacrifices, inside the מקדש,
phrases.notes: These are features that נותר and a טמא כהן serving have in common, but תרומה does not.

phrases.english: and the rules of פיגול and נותר!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 12's reason for choosing תרומה over נותר
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that תרומה is the better source because of its shared features
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נותר shares an equal number of features with our case, so it should be just as good a source, or better

steps.title: Plural wording breaks the tie
steps.stepSummary: Learning a plural 'desecration' from another plural 'desecration' is better, so תרומה wins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learning a plural 'desecrating' from a plural 'desecrating' is better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the pushback. Since the feature count is a tie, the matching plural wording decides the question in favor of תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources share four features with our case, so the count alone cannot decide. The words of desecration by תרומה and in our פסוק are both written in plural form, which makes them a closer match. So the גזירה שוה from תרומה stands, and the punishment stays מיתה, not כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: The word 'desecrate' written in plural form
Is better, preferred

steps.whatToRemember: A טמא כהן who served gets מיתה בידי שמים, learned from תרומה. When two possible sources tie, a closer match in the wording of the פסוק decides.

phrases.english: Desecration written in the plural
learned from desecration written in the plural is better.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pushback of step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since נותר shares as many features, maybe the punishment should be learned from there (כרת)
steps.terutzMaskana: Plural matching plural is the deciding factor, so we learn from תרומה (מיתה)

steps.title: Where do we learn the punishment for a טבול יום who served?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's list includes a טבול יום who served in the מקדש, and the גמרא asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טבול יום who served: from where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on the ברייתא's list of those who get מיתה בידי שמים. It asks for the source, which sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טבול יום is a person who was טמא, already went to the מקוה, but must wait until nightfall to be fully טהור. The ברייתא says if he served in the מקדש he gets death. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who went to the מקוה today but is waiting for nightfall to be fully טהור
Who served (did the עבודה in the מקדש)
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: A טבול יום who served: from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the טמא case to the next case in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for a טבול יום who served getting מיתה בידי שמים

steps.title: רבי סימאי finds a hint in the פסוק 'ולא יחללו'
steps.stepSummary: רבי סימאי teaches that the hint for a טבול יום who served comes from 'קדשים יהיו לאלהיהם ולא יחללו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי סימאי says, where is the hint that a טבול יום who served has desecrated the service? The פסוק says: 'They shall be holy to their God and they shall not desecrate.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא. רבי סימאי points to a פסוק about כהנים being holy and not desecrating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי סימאי calls it a רמז, a hint, because the פסוק does not openly say 'טבול יום'. He shows that the word 'desecrate' in this פסוק includes a טבול יום who served. The next step explains why this פסוק can be used for him.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא quoted in this ברייתא
A hint in the פסוק
He desecrated (made the service invalid)
The פסוק teaches

phrases.english: As it is taught: רבי סימאי says,
a hint for a טבול יום
that if he served he desecrated, from where?
The verse says:
"They shall be holy to their God and they shall not desecrate."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'קדשים יהיו לאלהיהם ולא יחללו' hints at the טבול יום who served

steps.title: Why this פסוק is free to teach about a טבול יום
steps.stepSummary: The טמא כהן who served is already learned from 'וינזרו', so 'ולא יחללו' can be applied to a טבול יום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק is not needed for a טמא who served, since we learn that from 'וינזרו', apply it to a טבול יום who served.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how it can use this פסוק for a טבול יום. The case of a fully טמא כהן is already covered by a different פסוק, so this one is free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally 'ולא יחללו' would seem to be about a טמא כהן. But a טמא כהן serving is already learned from 'וינזרו', so this פסוק is not needed there. Using the rule of 'אם אינו ענין', the extra פסוק is moved over to teach about the טבול יום.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this case
Apply it to a different case
We already learn it from
'And they shall keep away', the פסוק about טמאים separating from holy things

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different פסוקים with 'ולא יחללו'. רב יוסף's פסוק in step 10 is ויקרא 22:2, the 'וינזרו' פסוק, and it covers the טמא כהן. רבי סימאי's פסוק is ויקרא 21:6. Because the טמא case is already covered by 22:2, the פסוק in 21:6 is free to teach about the טבול יום.

phrases.english: If it is not needed for a טמא who served,
since we learn that from "and they shall keep away",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:2

phrases.english: apply it to a טבול יום who served.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the פסוק from step 16 can be used for a טבול יום
steps.kashyaTarget: The unstated problem that 'ולא יחללו' seems to be about a טמא כהן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving an extra פסוק to another case (אם אינו ענין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is about a fully טמא כהן, not a טבול יום
steps.terutzMaskana: The טמא case comes from 'וינזרו', so this פסוק teaches about the טבול יום

steps.title: The punishment is death, learned from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: Through a גזירה שוה on the word חילול from תרומה, a טבול יום who served gets מיתה בידי שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'desecration' here from 'desecration' by תרומה: just as there the punishment is death, so too here it is death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes by explaining how the תנא derives what punishment the טבול יום gets. It uses the same word link to תרומה that was used for a טמא כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only told us the טבול יום 'desecrates', not what his punishment is. The matching word חילול by תרומה, where the punishment is מיתה, fills in the punishment. So a טבול יום who served gets מיתה בידי שמים, just as the ברייתא's list said.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another through a matching word
There (in the other case)
So too here
Death (here, at the hands of Heaven)

steps.whatToRemember: A טבול יום who served gets מיתה בידי שמים: the פסוק 'ולא יחללו' includes him, and a גזירה שוה on חילול from תרומה gives the punishment.

phrases.english: And he learns 'desecration' from 'desecration' by תרומה,
just as there it is with death,
so too here it is with death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation by supplying the punishment
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A טבול יום who served is punished with מיתה בידי שמים, learned from תרומה through the word חילול

steps.title: Source for a כהן lacking his בגדים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a כהן who serves without his full בגדי כהונה gets מיתה בידי שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a כהן who is missing his priestly clothes, how do we know he is punished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on the ברייתא's list, a מחוסר בגדים, and asks for its source. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a כהן who serves without his בגדים gets מיתה בידי שמים. The גמרא wants a פסוק that makes this true, just as it found one for the טבול יום.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן missing one of his required priestly garments
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And one lacking vestments — from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the טבול יום, the גמרא moves to the next case in the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for מיתה for a מחוסר בגדים who served.

steps.title: The verse about girding them with a belt
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן, which some trace to רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון, brings the פסוק 'וחגרת אתם אבנט.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן, and some trace it to רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון: the פסוק says 'You shall gird them with a belt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק that is the source. It will explain how the פסוק works in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about dressing אהרן and his sons ends with 'and they shall have the כהונה.' This ties their כהונה to wearing the בגדים.

keyTerms.meaning: Some trace this teaching back to
The belt worn by the כהנים

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָטוּ בָּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: and some trace it in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon:
phrases.notes: Literally 'they reached it in his name.' Some people traced this teaching all the way back to him.

phrases.english: "You shall gird them with a belt."
phrases.notes: שמות 29:9

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 by naming the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק 'וחגרת אתם אבנט', which ties the כהונה to the בגדים.

steps.title: Without his בגדים, a כהן counts as a זר
steps.stepSummary: When the בגדים are on, the כהונה is on. Without them he is like a זר, and a זר who serves gets מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When their clothes are on them, their כהונה is on them. When their clothes are not on them, their כהונה is not on them. So they become like זרים, and we already learned that a זר who serves is punished with death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the פסוק and finishes the proof. A כהן without בגדים is treated like a non-כהן, so he gets a זר's punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links כהונה to wearing the בגדים. Without them, he is treated as a זר for this service. Since the ברייתא already said a זר ששימש gets מיתה, the same punishment applies to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Their status as כהנים
A non-כהן
A non-כהן who did the עבודה in the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: He does not stop being a כהן in general. The point is only that while serving without בגדים, he is treated like a זר.

phrases.english: At a time when their vestments are upon them —
their priesthood is upon them;
when their vestments are not upon them —
their priesthood is not upon them.
And so they are considered non-priests,
and the Master said: a non-priest who served — is punished with death.
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is the ברייתא itself, which listed the זר earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק from step 20 leads to the punishment.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מחוסר בגדים who serves is treated as a זר and gets מיתה בידי שמים.

steps.title: Source for one lacking atonement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a מחוסר כפרה who serves gets מיתה בידי שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And someone who is still missing his atonement offering, how do we know he is punished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the ברייתא and asks for its source. This sets up רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחוסר כפרה has already gone to the מקוה, but he still has not brought the קרבן that finishes his טהרה. The question is why serving in that state brings מיתה.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who has not yet brought the קרבן that completes his טהרה

phrases.english: And one lacking atonement — from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for מיתה for a מחוסר כפרה who served.

steps.title: Before the atonement offering, he is still somewhat impure
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא brings 'וכפר עליה הכהן וטהרה.' Only after the כפרה is she טהורה, so before it she is still טמאה. A טמא who serves gets מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: the פסוק says 'The כהן shall atone for her and she will be pure.' Saying she becomes pure shows she was impure until then. And we learned that a טמא who serves is punished with death.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא shows that a מחוסר כפרה still counts as a טמא, so he gets the punishment of a טמא who served.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says she becomes טהורה only after the כהן brings her קרבן. That means that until then she still has some טומאה. So a כהן in that state is like a טמא ששימש, whom the ברייתא already said gets מיתה.

keyTerms.meaning: And she will become pure
By implication, which shows that
An impure כהן who did the עבודה

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: for the verse says
"And the priest shall atone for her and she shall be pure."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:8, about a woman after childbirth.

phrases.english: "She shall be pure" — which implies that until now she is impure.
And the Master said: an impure one who served — is punished with death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מחוסר כפרה is still considered טמא until his קרבן, so he gets the punishment of a טמא ששימש.

steps.title: Source for one who did not wash hands and feet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a כהן who serves without washing his hands and feet gets מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a כהן who did not wash his hands and feet, how do we know he is punished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the next case in the ברייתא and asks for its source. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before serving, a כהן must wash his hands and feet from the כיור. The ברייתא says skipping this brings מיתה, and the גמרא wants the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Washing hands and feet before the עבודה

phrases.english: And one whose hands and feet are not washed,
from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for מיתה for a כהן who served without washing.

steps.title: They shall wash so that they will not die
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק itself says 'they shall wash with water so that they will not die,' so not washing brings מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'When they come into the אהל מועד, they shall wash with water so that they will not die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that states the punishment directly. No comparison to another case is needed here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier cases, which were compared to a זר or a טמא, here the פסוק itself says 'so that they will not die.' That means one who does not wash and serves is liable to מיתה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tent of Meeting, the משכן
So that they will not die

steps.whatToRemember: A מחוסר בגדים counts as a זר. A מחוסר כפרה counts as a טמא. A כהן who did not wash gets מיתה straight from the פסוק. All of them get מיתה בידי שמים.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"When they come into the Tent of Meeting
they shall wash with water so that they will not die."
phrases.notes: שמות 30:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק says 'wash so that they will not die,' which means not washing brings מיתה.

steps.title: Source for a drunk כהן getting מיתה
steps.stepSummary: A כהן who serves while drunk on wine gets מיתה, because the פסוק says 'do not drink wine… so that you do not die.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And a כהן who is drunk on wine gets מיתה, as it is written: 'Wine and strong drink do not drink, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the ברייתא's list and gives the source for the next case: a כהן who serves drunk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like with washing hands and feet in the step before, the פסוק itself mentions dying. So the punishment of מיתה is stated openly, and no extra derivation is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who drank wine (and are drunk)
Strong drink, other intoxicating drink
'Etc.': the פסוק continues beyond what is quoted

phrases.english: And those who are drunk on wine:
as it is written: 'Wine and strong drink do not drink, etc.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:9. The 'etc.' hides the key words at the end: 'so that you shall not die.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of sources for each case of מיתה in the ברייתא, following the pattern of the washing case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in ויקרא 10:9 explicitly ties drinking wine before service to dying.

steps.title: Overgrown hair compared to drinking wine
steps.stepSummary: A כהן with overgrown hair gets מיתה, because the פסוק about hair sits right next to the פסוק about wine, so they share the same punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a כהן with overgrown hair gets מיתה, as it is written: 'They shall not shave their heads, and they shall not let their hair grow long,' and right after it is written: 'And wine they shall not drink.' Overgrown hair is compared to being drunk on wine. Just as being drunk on wine brings מיתה, so too overgrown hair brings מיתה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for a כהן with overgrown hair. The פסוק about hair does not mention death, so the גמרא learns it from the next פסוק about wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hair פסוק has no punishment written in it. Because the wine פסוק comes right after it, the two are linked with a היקש. Since drinking wine brings מיתה, from the previous step, overgrown hair brings מיתה too.

keyTerms.meaning: Those whose hair is overgrown (uncut for a long time)
After it, right next to it
It is compared: a היקש, linking two things placed together
'Just as… so too…': the formula for carrying a law from one case to another

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that מיתה can come from a placement in the text (a היקש) and not only from a פסוק that openly says 'they will die.'

phrases.english: And those with overgrown hair on their heads:
as it is written: 'Their heads they shall not shave'
'and they shall not let their hair grow long,'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:20.

phrases.english: and it is written right after it: 'And wine they shall not drink.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:21, the very next פסוק.

phrases.english: Overgrown hair is compared to being drunk on wine:
just as those drunk on wine are punished with death,
so too those with overgrown hair are punished with death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 26: the מיתה for wine is now carried over to overgrown hair through a היקש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש between יחזקאל 44:20 (hair) and 44:21 (wine) gives overgrown hair the same מיתה as wine.

steps.title: Three cases that are only a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says an ערל, an אונן, and a כהן who serves sitting do not get מיתה. They only break an אזהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But an uncircumcised כהן, a mourner, and one who serves sitting are only under a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now switches from the cases of מיתה to a group of cases with a lighter punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אבל ('but') marks the contrast: these three cases are also forbidden, but they are not on the list of מיתה בידי שמים. They are only a plain prohibition, an אזהרה.

keyTerms.meaning: An uncircumcised man
A mourner on the day a close relative died
Sitting, serving while seated
A warning, a plain prohibition without מיתה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think these cases are allowed. They are still forbidden. The only difference is the punishment: no מיתה בידי שמים.

phrases.english: But an uncircumcised one, a mourner, one who sits —
are under a prohibition.
phrases.notes: He means only a prohibition, not the מיתה of the earlier cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the whole list of מיתה cases sourced in the steps before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ערל, אונן, and יושב who serve are only under an אזהרה, not מיתה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that an ערל may not serve?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that an uncircumcised כהן is forbidden to serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: An uncircumcised כהן: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the three אזהרה cases and asks for the source for the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case in the ברייתא needs a source, just like the מיתה cases had. Here the question is only about the prohibition itself, since there is no מיתה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: An uncircumcised one: from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first case listed in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that an uncircumcised כהן is forbidden to do the עבודה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: we learned it from יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says this law is not found in the Torah of משה. It was taught by the נביא יחזקאל, who said that no one 'uncircumcised of heart' may enter the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This matter we did not learn from the Torah of משה רבינו, until יחזקאל son of בוזי came and taught us: 'Any foreigner, uncircumcised of heart…'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the source for an ערל is a פסוק in יחזקאל, not in the חמשה חומשי תורה. The quote continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unusually, the source here is from נביאים. רב חסדא openly says we would not know this from the Torah of משה alone. The פסוק being quoted speaks of 'uncircumcised of heart', and the rest of it comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah of משה our teacher
The נביא יחזקאל, son of בוזי
A foreigner
Uncircumcised of heart

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר זֶה מִתּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לֹא לָמַדְנוּ,
phrases.english: This matter we did not learn from the Torah of Moshe our teacher,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁבָּא יְחֶזְקֵאל בֶּן בּוּזִי וְלִמְּדָנוּ:
phrases.english: until Yechezkel son of Buzi came and taught us:
'Any foreigner, uncircumcised of heart'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:9. The פסוק keeps going in the next part of the גמרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר זֶה מִתּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לֹא לָמַדְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The prohibition on an ערל serving comes from the נביא יחזקאל (44:9), not from the Torah of משה.
